column1: # Obligation citations — goal 0008 (OpenCode source continuation).
# One row per rule of this increment that a gate-runnable Go test discharges, in the four id spaces the
# increment's rules come from:
#   D1–D4   the goal's four `Done when` clauses, in order
#           (docs/goals/0008-opencode-source-continuation.md);
#   B1–B2   the goal's two `Bounds` clauses, in order;
#   S1–S6   the rules of AGENTS.md's OpenCode-source paragraph ("OpenCode is a source whose session is a row
#           in that harness's own store"), in the paragraph's own order — the inherited provider and its two
#           reference forms; the read's own answers (the rendering, no trace text, no dialogue projection);
#           the progress event beside the terminal one; the session controls the read does not hold; the
#           container-member boundary; the committed fixture document;
#   E1      the failure half of the same interface (the goal's fourth clause asks for the error answer too:
#           an OpenCode reference the provider cannot resolve is the established not-found failure).
# scripts/obligation-citations.py is the arbiter: every row's cited test must exist in the named package
# and run and pass, and the `citations` step is required — a tree that lost this file, or a citation that
# went stale, fails the gate instead of passing partially. Columns: rule_id, test, package, artifact.
# Tab-separated; `#` comments and blank lines are ignored; a rule id appears once.
# Deliberately not covered, with the reason (form-based: a row is one Go test in a package
# scripts/gate-targets.txt covers, so a rule whose gate evidence is a python case the required `selftest`
# step runs, or a native harness run, cannot hold one):
#   S7 — the native direction's own discipline (the harness's own importer plants the fixture; the CLI is
#          driven at the *load* level; the installed Codex rollout's own records are compared with the
#          fixture document's own bytes, one output per call; the printed Codex line is read as a POSIX
#          invocation; a requested turn is recorded as what the harness answered). Its evidence is the
#          native run scripts/opencode-native-check.py and the python cases
#          scripts/tests/test_opencode_native_check.py the `selftest` step runs — a native harness run and a
#          python case, not a Go test.
# Two evidence halves belong to clauses whose rows hold their Go-test half; they are named here rather than
# dropped: D1's "provide an actual target native load/resume result" is the native run's `verification.load`
# (Codex's own `thread/resume`, quoted in the record), and D3's "source-side AgentsView packages and SQLite
# schema are unchanged" is the gate's required `parity` step (scripts/upstream-parity.py), while its
# "the accepted OpenCode-target route and prior Claude/Codex routes remain correct" half is the accepted
# routes' own suites the gate's `test` step runs (D3's row cites the OpenCode-target route's own case, and
# the record's §4 quotes the two native checks' runs).
